real_estate.homebuilder: Rents rose nationally for the first time since 2023; here they are up 4% to 9% from a year ago.
real_estate.commentary:
Friday's selloff pulled mortgage rates down with Treasury yields. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average fell 0.12 to 7.33%, with the 15-year at 6.89%, and Freddie Mac's weekly survey on Thursday was 7.28%. On today's $1,242,321 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $6,834 a month in principal and interest.

Realtor.com's October rental report shows the median asking rent for 0 to 2 bedroom units in the 50 largest metros at $1,692, up 0.1% from a year ago, the first annual increase since June 2023. Here the climb is steeper (chart): Zillow's rent index has Milpitas up 9.4%, Union City 7.1%, Fremont 6.8%, Newark 5.5% and Hayward 3.9%, against 2.9% nationally on the same measure.

In realtor.com's latest weekly data, homes for sale are up 8.3% from a year ago, new listings are down 10.3%, and the median list price is down 1.2%, the 43rd straight week below last year. Its new construction report finds builders holding their prices while existing home prices slip.

Here, supply is up 3% from this date last year across the 14 cities in both of our exports (1,710 from 1,659), while homes in contract are down 29% (567 from 803). New homes are the ones giving ground: the board's median new listing (built 2025 or 2026) asks $1,249,000, down from $1,382,750 for the newest homes a year ago, while resale rose to $899,694 from $825,000. Part of that is mix, since many new homes are townhomes.

Saturday's export shows 2,262 board wide, from 2,313 Thursday, with 125 coming soon and 102 brand new. The five city ledger is 565, from 589 Thursday: Hayward (161) fell nine, Milpitas (88) six, and Fremont (194), Newark (69) and Union City (53) three each.

What this means for you: renters, local rents are rising faster than the national headline, so price out a purchase before your lease renews. Buyers, rates just eased and fewer people are signing contracts, so there is room to negotiate.

• Board wide: 2,262 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 125 coming soon and 102 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 565 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 501 are on the market and 64 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 194 live, 159 active, 24 coming soon and 10 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,242,321 at $769 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 40 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 161, Milpitas 88, Newark 69, Union City 53.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,000,000 at $667 a square foot. 250 homes are priced under a million, and 179 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Cards are Friday's close against Thursday's. Markets are closed for the weekend.
stocks.news:
Friday's close: the S&P 500 fell 3.70%, the Dow 1.93% and the Nasdaq 5.28%, after Thursday's drop of about 2% across the board. For the week the Nasdaq lost 10.0% and the Dow 8.0%, both their worst weeks since March 2020, and the S&P 500 lost 8.6%, its worst since April 2025 (chart). The S&P 500 is now 11.6% below its October 6 record and the Dow 11.4% below its August 5 record, both in correction territory, and the Nasdaq is 18.1% off its high and below where it started the year.

Chips led the fall. Santa Clara's Nvidia dropped 14.01% to $125.53 on reports that SEC staff are examining its accounting, which neither the SEC nor Nvidia has confirmed; it lost 22.9% on the week. AMD fell 13.25% and Broadcom 12.19%, and the VIX fear gauge closed at 35.89, its highest since April 2025. Anthropic, which priced at $83, closed its first day Thursday at $97.17 and fell 8.50% Friday to $88.91, still above the offer price. A week to remember for all the wrong reasons.

feature_image.alt: Line chart of how far each index closed below its record, daily from Sept. 1 to Nov. 20, 2026, with lines at 10% (correction) and 20% (bear market). On Nov. 20 the S&P 500 was 11.6% below its Oct. 6 record, the Dow 11.4% below its Aug. 5 record and the Nasdaq 18.1% below its Oct. 6 record.
feature_image.caption: The S&P 500 and Dow are in correction territory, and the Nasdaq is 18% off its high.

economy.note: Cards are Friday's settlements: the 10-Year from Treasury, gold and silver December COMEX futures, Brent ICE front month (January).
economy.commentary:
Investors ran to bonds. The 10-Year Treasury closed Friday at 4.92%, down 0.12 on the day and down from 5.07% on Wednesday, and that is what pulled mortgage rates lower.

Metals did not offer shelter. Gold settled Friday at $3,515.40, down 4.62%, and silver at $41.07, down 7.41%, as selling spread beyond stocks. Brent settled at $92.57, up 0.64%. When gold falls with stocks, someone needed cash.

crypto.commentary: Bitcoin slipped below $60,000 during Friday's selloff and is near $60,156 this afternoon, up 2.30% over the past 24 hours, live from CoinGecko at 3:52 PM PT. Ether is near $1,682.78 (+3.95%) and XRP near $0.93 (+2.51%). A small weekend bounce after a rough week.
